Deep-sea footage from a remotely operated vehicle. Pale mineral chimneys rise from the dark sea floor. Cloudy plumes pour from their tops and drift away. Close up, a thin white stream jets from an opening in the rock. Pale crabs and shrimp crowd the chimney walls. A caption reads MARIANIS TRENCH HYDROTHERMAL VENTS.
csv	content_ch10_cc_openers.csv	The Deep-Sea Vent	Answer	Water molecules in the hot stream move fast, and many have enough energy to escape into vapor. But a bubble can only form if the vapor inside it pushes back as hard as the water pressing on it. Deep down, the weight of the water above squeezes the molecules together and keeps them from spreading apart into vapor. That pressure is very large, so the water must be much hotter before its vapor pressure is high enough to open a bubble. In shallower water the pressure is lower, so the water reaches its boiling point at a lower temperature, and it fizzes.

csv	content_ch10_cc_openers.csv	The Syringe Boiling Trick	Answer	Water molecules at the surface keep escaping into vapor. At this temperature they have a set vapor pressure. Pulling the plunger lowers the external pressure on the water. When that external pressure falls to the water's vapor pressure, molecules inside the liquid can escape into bubbles of vapor, so the water boils. The molecules already have enough energy; no heat is added.

When the two rates are equal, the amounts stop changing, but both reactions keep running. So some nitrogen and hydrogen are always left.

csv	content_ch14_buffer_openers.csv	Half a Buffer	Answer	Ammonia alone: NH₃ is a weak base; it cannot consume OH⁻, and its own NH₄⁺ is only about 1.3 × 10⁻³ M, so the added OH⁻ stays mostly free. csv	content_ch14_titration_openers.csv	The Vinegar Lab	Answer	At equivalence all CH₃COOH has reacted: CH₃COOH + OH⁻ → CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O. The flask holds Na⁺, CH₃COO⁻ (0.044 M in the total volume) and water. Acetate is a weak base, Kb = Kw ÷ Ka = 5.6 × 10⁻¹⁰: CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COOH + OH⁻; [OH⁻] ≈ 5.0 × 10⁻⁶ M; pH ≈ 8.70. With HCl, the flask holds Na⁺ and Cl⁻; Cl⁻ is not a base, so the pH is 7.00.

csv	content_ch15_complex_openers.csv	The Disappearing Precipitate	Answer	NH₃ (Lewis base, lone pair) binds Ag⁺ (Lewis acid): Ag⁺ + 2NH₃ ⇌ Ag(NH₃)₂⁺, Kf 1.7 × 10⁷ (OpenStax 15.2). Free Ag⁺ falls far below what AgCl's Ksp allows, so AgCl keeps dissolving (coupled equilibria). With ammonia in excess, free [Ag⁺] = Kd [complex] ÷ [NH₃]², millions of times less than the silver present.

csv	content_ch16_equilibrium_G_openers.csv	The Pressurized Reactor	Answer	Q = P(N₂) × P(H₂)³ ÷ P(NH₃)² = 8.17 × 10⁻⁵. Q far below 1 lowers ΔG, but not enough. (OpenStax Example 16.12.)

csv	content_ch16_free_energy_openers.csv	The Hand Warmer	Answer	4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃: ΔH° = −1648.4 kJ (strongly exothermic); ΔS° = −550.0 J/K (gas consumed). ΔG° = ΔH° − TΔS° = −1648.4 − 298 × (−0.5500) = −1484.5 kJ, matching ΣνΔG°f (−1484.4 kJ). Enthalpy wins: the large negative ΔH° outweighs the entropy penalty, and the released enthalpy warms the hands.

csv	content_ch16_free_energy_openers.csv	Water Won't Boil at Room Temperature	Answer	H₂O(l) → H₂O(g): ΔH° = +44.01 kJ; ΔS° = +118.8 J/K = 0.1188 kJ/K; ΔG° = 44.01 − 298 × 0.1188 = +8.6 kJ (from ΔG°f: +8.5 kJ). Anions in the salt bridge drift toward the zinc. E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.337 − (−0.7618) = 1.099 V.

csv	content_ch17_nernst_openers.csv	The Daniell Cell Runs Down	Answer	Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, n = 2, Q = [Zn²⁺]/[Cu²⁺]. E = E° − (0.0592/2) log Q.
